That said, the conversations reinforced that short, defined sprints to build security can be necessary, but they should have clear timelines, protected non‑negotiables, and tight emergency rules so work never becomes the whole of life.

text: There should be a balance between work and spare time for other things.
llm_text: I disagree — work shouldn't always come first, even if it costs spare time. After decades in finance I've learned faith, family, health, and community keep life whole; I work to provide, but not at the expense of relationships or my spiritual rest (Sundays/Mass). Short sprints of extra effort can be necessary, but they must be time‑bound, negotiated, and balanced with protected rest to avoid burnout.
